tail_analysis.reading: THE TYPICAL EVENT LOSES MONEY. Median -4.49% vs SPY over a quarter; 40% positive. The +1.19% mean is entirely a 10% right tail -- 40 events summing to +3,427%, seven times the total positive mass. Remove them and the other 366 average -8.05%. This is a losing strategy with a lottery-ticket tail, not a signal with noise around it. It worsened with more data exactly as a null does: spec #1 median -0.17% -> spec #2 -4.49%, hit rate 49% -> 40%. Not tradeable in reverse either: the +269% events are what a short book cannot survive. No instrument improvement fixes this -- matched controls, winsorizing, fixing survivorship, a longer horizon, a larger sample all push the median DOWN. The problem is the shape of the outcome distribution, not the measurement of it. And the universe is survivor-biased upward, so the true median is worse than -4.49%.
tail_analysis.implication_for_spec_3: Any hypothesis that is a bet on WHICH small company recovers will have this shape. A third specification must have a mechanism where the MEDIAN outcome is positive -- slow information diffusion (post-earnings drift) or a mechanical flow (index-deletion rebound), not a fundamental bet on survival. Filters on insider buying -- officers only, larger threshold, first buy in N years -- are variations on a distribution that has now failed at two horizons and two sample sizes, not new hypotheses.

params.hypothesis: POST-EARNINGS-ANNOUNCEMENT DRIFT. Small-cap prices underreact to earnings news, so a large positive announcement-window abnormal return is followed by continued positive drift over the next quarter. Direction is LONG-ONLY and pre-registered: positive surprises only. The short leg is NOT tested here, and testing it later is a SEPARATE specification consuming another slot.
params.universe: 907 US primary-exchange common stocks, 250k <= ADV <= 5M, price >= $2, >= 200 bars (UNCHANGED from v1/v2; frozen data/universe/v27_universe.csv)
params.event_source: SEC EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 ('Results of Operations and Financial Condition'), taken from the submissions API's structured `items` field; ticker->CIK rebuilt from EDGAR full-text search. NOT Finnhub: its earnings endpoint caps at 4 quarters and carries no announcement date (probe run 33938076855). www.sec.gov is 403 from CI AND from the operator's machine; data.sec.gov and efts.sec.gov answer only a User-Agent with no URL in it (probe run 33939274269).
params.event_window: 2023-09-01 .. 2026-09-05; one announcement per ticker per filing date (an 8-K and its same-day amendment are one event)
params.announcement_day_A: acceptanceDateTime is served in UTC; convert to ET, DST-aware. A = the filing day D when D is a trading day and acceptance precedes its 16:00 ET close (this covers pre-market and intraday). Otherwise A = the next trading day after D. Measured on the probe: 66.5% after the close, 26.2% pre-market, 7.4% intraday.
params.surprise_measure: ANNOUNCEMENT-WINDOW ABNORMAL RETURN (Chan-Jegadeesh-Lakonishok 1996), NOT an analyst-estimate SUE -- no free consensus exists at this universe size. CAR = the compounded stock return over sessions [A, A+1] MINUS the compounded SPY return over those same two sessions.
params.selection_threshold: CAR[A, A+1] >= +5.0%. ABSOLUTE, and fixed HERE, before the CAR distribution has ever been computed. Deliberately not a cross-sectional decile (whose peer ranking would include later events) and not a trailing-window percentile (which would burn a year of the sample warming up). An absolute bar is point-in-time by construction.
params.entry: the first bar STRICTLY AFTER the close of A+1 -- the open of A+2. event_ts is therefore SET TO the close of A+1 so that the engine's existing look-ahead guard produces this entry with no new code path. Entering at A+1's close would trade on the second day of the selection window itself.
params.independence: qt event-study _dedupe_overlaps, unchanged: the FIRST qualifying event per ticker wins, and any later event whose 63-bar window overlaps it is dropped. Quarterly reporting against a 63-bar hold means announcements nearly TILE, so expect heavy dropping -- roughly one surviving event per ticker per two quarters.
params.delisting_handling: recorded at LAST TRADED PRICE and flagged exit_status=delisted; NOT -100%; three-way survivorship sensitivity required with the number (UNCHANGED)
params.output_ledger: data/events/event_study_v3.csv -- NEVER data/events/event_study.csv (v1, frozen) and NEVER data/events/event_study_v2.csv (v2, frozen)
params.expected_n: ~7,292 matured announcements projected universe-wide (probe run 33939274269, 150-name sample). Even a pessimistic 5% qualification rate at the +5.0% bar gives ~365 events before dedup and ~180 after -- more than 4x the N>=40 floor. THIS IS WHAT MAKES AN ABSOLUTE THRESHOLD SAFE: N would have to arrive four times below a pessimistic estimate before the floor were in question.
params.why_this_is_not_a_variation_of_spec_1_or: Specs #1 and #2 bet on WHICH small company recovers, and produced a median-negative, tail-dominated distribution twice (see form4_cluster_buy_v2.result.read.tail_analysis). This bets instead on SLOW DIFFUSION OF PUBLIC INFORMATION: a mechanism whose claimed median is positive, whose event is a SCHEDULED PUBLIC DISCLOSURE rather than a discretionary private act, and whose event count is roughly thirteen times larger. Different event class, different mechanism, different failure mode.

caveats_to_travel_with_any_number: SHORT-TERM REVERSAL IS A HEADWIND BUILT INTO THE SELECTION. Buying after a >= +5% two-day move means buying into a move that may partly mean-revert. This biases the result DOWNWARD. It is not a flaw to be fixed but the honest price of using the price reaction as the surprise proxy, and it is why entry is A+2 rather than A+1.
PEAD IS THE MOST-PUBLISHED ANOMALY IN THE LITERATURE. Fifty years of publication is fifty years of arbitrage. A prior ABOVE the 15% project prior would be difficult to defend.

SURVIVORSHIP: unchanged and still unfixable free. Today's listed universe only; three years of small-cap delistings absent; biases UPWARD. probe_delisted.py: 0/3 bankruptcies serve price history. Any pass is a CEILING with an unknown floor.

THE UNIVERSE SCREEN IS NOT POINT-IN-TIME FOR EVENT SELECTION: names were screened on ADV as of 2026-09, so a 2023 announcement is selected using a liquidity fact from 2026. Unchanged from v1/v2, and it biases UPWARD.
23% OF THE UNIVERSE CONTRIBUTES NO EVENTS -- funds, foreign issuers filing 6-K, shells. A real exclusion rather than a data gap, but it narrows the effective universe below 907.

ONE PARAMETER FAMILY, ONE TEST. Threshold, window, horizon and direction are all fixed above. Changing ANY of them after the read is a NEW specification consuming another slot; qt.referee.declare refuses to silently redefine a declared spec.
